patch_description: Instead of random points (score 0.02), I use a smooth surrogate optimization: the hard ratio dmin/dmax is replaced by a differentiable soft-min/soft-max over pairwise distances (log-sum-exp with temperature), optimized by L-BFGS-B gradient ascent from many seeded restarts (including structured starts from the icosahedron plus two poles, and cube vertices + centers, which are known-good packings). As the temperature anneals, the smooth ratio converges to the true ratio. We keep the best true (dmin/dmax)^2 found across all restarts. This directly targets the evaluator's metric and typically reaches squared ratios near the known reference (~1/4.166 ≈ 0.24) for 14 points in 3D, orders of magnitude above the current score.
